# OpenCode Voice **Local-first voice dictation for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) (v2).** Press **F9**, speak, press **F9** again — your words appear as an editable draft in the chat you recorded from. Submit sends, esc discards, dictating again extends the draft. If anything goes wrong, **`ctrl+f9`** brings your last take back (see [Recovery](#recovery-ctrlf9)). > **Status:** early release (0.x). Linux only, tested mainly with PipeWire. > Expect rough edges; see [Current limitations](#current-limitations-and-planned-work).

  

## Your voice stays on your machine This plugin is built around one rule: **nothing you say ever leaves your computer.** Whisper runs locally, in-process, via [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx). There are no cloud speech APIs, no accounts, no API keys, no telemetry, and no server of mine or anyone else's involved in transcription. The plugin talks to the network in three cases, and none of them carries audio or transcript text: - opening the model manager fetches the list of available whisper models from k2-fsa's release page - confirming a download fetches that model file - once per day, unless disabled under Behavior, it fetches this package's public npm metadata to check for a newer version; it only informs you and never installs an update After a model is installed the plugin works fully offline (disable the optional update check to make no automatic request), on air-gapped machines and on confidential codebases. See [Data & privacy](#data--privacy) for exactly what is stored on disk. A remote transcription backend may be added in a future version. If it is, it will be opt-in and off by default. Local stays the default. ## Features - **Local and offline transcription** — speech processing never uses the network; model downloads are explicit and the metadata-only update check is optional - **Push-to-talk** (F9 by default) with a live level meter in the sidebar panel - **Proofread-before-send**: transcripts arrive as a prefilled form — edit, submit, or discard; a new take extends the open draft - **Model manager**: curated whisper models (tiny → medium, English and multilingual), downloaded on demand, switchable any time. Before a download starts, the plugin checks that the model directory is writable, that `tar` can read the archive, and how much room the install needs; a problem is named in one sentence, low space asks instead of refusing - **Voice activity detection**: pauses become line breaks, silence is never decoded - **Noise-annotation filter**: whisper artifacts like `(buzzing)` or `[BLANK_AUDIO]` are dropped before they reach your chat - **Filler-only lines**: a line that is nothing but `uh`, `um`, `hmm`… is dropped; words inside a line are never touched. The list is a setting (Advanced → Cleanup), so other languages can use their own fillers; `off` disables it. Enable debug logging to see what was dropped - **Loss-resistant safety net**: audio is kept until its draft is safely stored, and the draft until it is submitted; one key recovers either after a failure or crash - **Settings-first design**: shortcuts, language, VAD tuning, model RAM residency, and meter style all live in one menu (`ctrl+alt+v`) - **Update awareness**: the panel shows the installed version and marks an available release; each new release is announced once, never auto-installed - **Multi-terminal safe**: transcripts land only in the terminal that recorded them ### Update notifications The panel shows the installed Voice version, and the plugin can announce newer published versions with their complete release notes. The plugin itself never installs anything. Installing is OpenCode's job: it resolves the plugin entry in your `opencode.json` when it starts and picks up a newer published version on its own, so the announcement tells you what the next restart brings. You can also run it by hand: ```sh opencode plugin update @juliuskb/opencode-voice ``` Automatic checks happen at launch at most once per day. **Check for updates** can be disabled under Behavior; this stops automatic checks, indicators, and release notifications. A manual **Check for updates now** action remains available. Re-enabling automatic checks clears the cached update state and starts fresh. Failed offline checks may retry on a later launch after the backoff period. **Update channel** (Advanced → Debug, default `latest`) is the npm dist-tag the check follows. Set it to the same tag your `opencode.json` installs from, for example `next` for `"@juliuskb/opencode-voice@next"`; the plugin cannot see which tag OpenCode uses. Entering a tag makes one request to npm to verify it exists (even when **Check for updates** is off; nothing else is sent), and changing it clears the cached update state. ## Requirements - **Linux** (macOS/Windows planned). Audio capture requires `pw-record` (PipeWire), `arecord` (ALSA), or `ffmpeg`; archive extraction requires `tar` with bzip2 support. These are already present on most distributions. - OpenCode. Tested with OpenCode 2.1.1; older versions are likely to work, since the plugin uses only the public plugin API and OpenCode's bundled Bun runtime, but they are not tested. Each release's notes name the OpenCode version it was verified on. - ~110 MB–1.9 GB disk per model (downloaded on first run, your choice of size). ## Performance Transcription runs on the CPU, and the bar is low. This plugin is developed and used daily on a mid-range 2018 ultrabook: an Intel i5-8265U (4 cores, 8 threads) with 12 GB of RAM. Measured there with the recommended `small.en` model on 6 threads: | `small.en`, i5-8265U, 6 threads | | |---|---| | transcription time | 0.25 to 0.5 × the length of the take (a 20 s take comes back in 5 to 10 s) | | model load, first take | 2 to 4 s, then kept in RAM (Behavior → Model residency) | | memory while the model is loaded | about 0.8 GB, measured in isolation | | memory after the model unloads | 0.35 to 0.45 GB stays with the allocator; repeated load/unload cycles do not grow it | The `R` figure in the panel is the memory of the whole OpenCode server process, not the plugin's share. *Unload model from memory now* in the settings menu frees the model's part immediately. Anything newer or with more cores is faster. On weaker hardware, `base.en` or `tiny.en` trade some accuracy for speed; the model manager shows the size of each. Thread count is a setting if you want to leave cores free. More measurements will be added here as the plugin runs on more machines. If you have figures from yours, the model, CPU, and the transcription time for a take of known length are all it takes; open an issue with them. GPU-accelerated transcription is not supported and is not planned until the CPU path is fully stable. It may come later. ## Install Add the package to your opencode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`): ```json { "plugins": ["@juliuskb/opencode-voice"] } ``` opencode installs it automatically on next start.
From source (development) ```sh git clone https://github.com/JuliusKB/opencode-voice cd opencode-voice && bun install ``` Then point your config at the directory: ```json { "plugins": ["/path/to/opencode-voice"] } ``` Before opening a pull request, run the checks: ```sh bun run check # strict type check bun test # guard tests, including a compile check of the panel bun run build # compiles the panel to dist/tui.js (what npm users receive) ``` The local checkout runs the panel from source; the published package ships it precompiled, because OpenCode compiles plugin files inside `node_modules` differently and a source `.tsx` panel would render once and never update.
## First run 1. Start opencode — the **Voice** panel appears in the sidebar showing "no model installed". 2. Press **F9** — the model manager opens. Pick one (`small.en` is the recommended default for English; `small` for multilingual) and confirm the download. Progress shows in the panel. 3. When it's ready, press **F9**, speak, **F9** again. Your transcript opens as a form: **submit sends it to the chat, esc discards.**

That's the entire setup. ## Usage | Key | Action | |---|---| | `F9` | start / stop recording (configurable) | | `esc` while recording | cancel the take | | `ctrl+alt+v` | settings menu (configurable) | | `ctrl+f9` | restore a saved draft or retry a failed take (configurable) | | command palette → "Restore last transcript" | same recovery action | Your transcript arrives as a form in the chat. Edit it, then **enter** sends, **esc** discards: ![Transcript draft form: submit sends, esc discards](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusKB/opencode-voice/main/pics/form_unsubmitted.png) Dictating while a draft form is open **extends** it (blank line between takes). Note: manual edits typed into the form are lost when a new take extends it — edit last, or submit between takes. ## Recovery: `ctrl+f9` Nothing you dictate should be lost, even when something breaks. The plugin keeps your last take on disk until it is safely in a draft, and the draft until you submit it (details under [Data & privacy](#data--privacy)). **`ctrl+f9`**, or "Restore last transcript" in the command palette, brings it back: - after a failed transcription: re-transcribes the saved audio - after a crash, a restart, or an accidental esc: re-raises the saved draft in the chat you are in - if both exist: restores the draft, then appends the re-transcribed take Press it whenever a recording or draft disappears. "Nothing to restore" means there was nothing on disk. The key is configurable under Shortcuts. ## Settings `ctrl+alt+v` opens the menu. The main page covers daily use:

- **Transcription** — model (opens the model manager), language (for multilingual models; auto-detect by default) - **Audio** — input device, capture tool (with per-machine availability) - **Behavior** — model RAM residency, notification verbosity, the daily update check (on/off), the safety net, queue-vs-steer delivery - **Shortcuts** — all key bindings - **More** — Advanced settings, log viewer, update check, release notes, model unload, reset, **About** (version and the project's GitHub and npm pages) **Advanced…** holds the tuned-by-default knobs: decode chunking, transcript cleanup (the noise-annotation filter and the filler-word list), VAD sensitivity, level-meter style/size/rate, toast timings, debug logging, the update channel. Changed values are marked `*` with their recommended value shown; clearing a field reverts to it; one action resets everything. ## Data & privacy Everything lives in `~/.local/share/opencode-voice/`: - `models/` — downloaded whisper models (from k2-fsa's GitHub releases) - `settings.json` — your settings - `updates.json` — cached public version metadata and the last release notice shown (never audio, transcripts, or machine identifiers) - `voice.log` (+ `.prev`) — plugin log, current and previous run. **Never contains speech content or transcripts** at any log level. - `last-take.wav` / `last-draft.txt` — the **safety net** (on by default, Behavior → Safety net): your last take is kept on disk until it is assured delivered — the audio until transcription succeeds, then the draft text until you actually submit it. One slot, overwritten per take, deleted the moment delivery completes. If transcription fails or opencode crashes with a draft open, the restore key (`ctrl+f9`) recovers it: re-raises the saved draft, or re-transcribes the saved audio. Turning the setting off deletes both files (an active recording is removed as soon as the recorder releases it). With the safety net enabled, audio is recorded directly to `last-take.wav` and deleted only after its draft is safely stored. With it disabled, audio uses a temporary WAV and is deleted after transcription. Opening the model manager checks k2-fsa's GitHub release catalog; model files are downloaded from GitHub only after your explicit confirmation. Audio and transcripts are never sent with those requests. The optional daily update check requests only this package's public metadata from npm. Disable **Check for updates** under Behavior to make no such request; the only remaining one is the single verification when you type a new update channel yourself. **Deleting the directory above is a complete uninstall of all plugin data.** ## Troubleshooting - The log page (settings menu → *Show log*) shows what the plugin is doing; enable *Debug logging* (Advanced → Debug) for pipeline detail. - "nothing heard" or empty transcripts: check your system input level. The panel meter should move clearly while you speak; if it barely moves, raise the microphone level in your system settings. The meter gain setting only changes the display, not what Whisper hears. - "no recorder found": install PipeWire (`pw-record`), ALSA utils (`arecord`), or `ffmpeg`. The Recorder setting shows what's detected. - Transcription quality issues: try a larger model, or set the language explicitly instead of auto-detect (multilingual models only). ## Current limitations and planned work No unresolved server-crash issue is currently known. - **Drafts live in OpenCode's form dialog**, which was not designed for this. An earlier private version of this tool, built for OpenCode v1, appended the transcript straight into the prompt box through the v1 HTTP API (`/tui/append-prompt` and `/tui/submit-prompt`). OpenCode v2 removed those endpoints and does not expose an equivalent to plugins, so the form is the workaround. Consequences: edits you type into the form are lost when a new take extends it, and the form takes keyboard focus from whatever dialog was open. A cleaner delivery path (appending to the prompt again) depends on OpenCode exposing one. I intend to request that upstream once I have exhausted what the current plugin API can do and am sure I am not asking for something that already exists. Until then, this is the known rough spot. - macOS and Windows audio capture are not implemented. - **Live transcription** is planned: sliding-window partials will give a live, revisable transcript while recording, with the final transcript retaining the current proofread-before-send flow. ## Who made this I am a coding enthusiast, not a professional developer. My background is Python, not TypeScript. I built this plugin for my own daily use first; it solved a problem for me, and I am publishing it because it may solve the same problem for someone else. ## How this was built and tested I can read and review this code, but I did not write it fluently by hand: it was written with AI assistance and reviewed by me. What I vouch for is **behavior**. Every feature in this README has been exercised as a user would exercise it, on a real machine with real microphones: recording, transcribing, extending drafts, switching models, cancelling downloads, recovering a failed take. A small set of automated tests covers the guards that protect your data (model path safety, settings validation, draft handling). Because everything runs locally, the blast radius of a bug is small: a lost take, a bad transcript, a crashed panel. The safety net exists so a lost take can be recovered. The one risk local design does not remove is a compromised dependency, and that one is shared by every npm package you install. Found a bug or a behavior that contradicts this README? [Open an issue](https://github.com/JuliusKB/opencode-voice/issues) with what you did and what happened. ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © JuliusKB --- *Built for OpenCode, using OpenCode.*
